## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `33b946d34d087b6a60e3a1a5e3ac6d3f64f8f98c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0085-object-semantic-roles-over-surface-hint-blocks.md + none
Security-touching: no

Read for this record: card #37800 (body and its 4 comments), PR #38010 (body, file list, net diff against merge base `30a8047bad6e264762dd41ded7f1290c1224afc6`, which is also `main` as fetched at 15:40Z), comments 7209608089 (on #37792) and 7209632085 (on #37800), the bodies and threads of #37792 and #37802, and the check-runs on the head. The compare API reports the head 1 ahead, 0 behind, one file, +31/-0.

### ① Derived judgments

- The diff is one blockquote Note in ADR-0085 §2, placed after the 2026-11-23 `actionLayout` Note and before `### 3. Deletions`. No heading, no schema, no package, no skill, no generated file. It changes no accept-set and no public surface: right.
- The Note says neither key is in the spec yet. On `main`, `pinOverview` has 0 hits in the whole tree and `fieldTabs` has 0 hits outside `ui/` (20 files under `ui/`, all the form-level key). `ObjectSchemaBase` is a `strictObject` (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`), and `ObjectSchema` is built on it. So the Note admits two keys the spec still refuses, and says so: right.
- Not teaching the keys in `skills/**` in this PR (the card's step 2) is right for the same reason: a skill would teach a key `os validate` refuses. The claim moved that step to #37792 and #37802, and the carrier note 7222282212 on #37802 is posted.
- CI on this head, read at 15:41Z: every non-skipped run is `success` except `Test Core (1/10)`, which was still `in_progress` and was not waited for. The gates that judge this Note are green: `Lint · docs & code guards` (the symbol-anchor gate), `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (ADR anchors, ADR index), `Check Documentation Links` (ADR links), `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check Changeset`. On the first read at 15:38Z, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` and `Lint · repo & tooling gates` were also pending; both finished `success`.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body, label `skip-changeset`, no changeset in the diff, `Check Changeset` green. An ADR-only diff publishes nothing, so this is right. The `Metadata-protocol: added` entries belong to #37792 and #37802, where the keys enter the spec, and both cards already say so.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` in the dev report (7222225966): empty. Nothing to escalate.
- Deviation "step 2 (skills) not in this PR": accepted, see ①.
- Deviation "Note length, 30 lines against 19": answered in ④, the length is earned.
- Deviation "shallow checkout, dates read from the cards": accepted. Every date and time in the Note is on the card bodies.
- The two out-of-scope findings are carried: the `fieldTabs` homonym on #37802 (7222282212), the `recordPageColumns.ts` header rewrite already in #37792 step 3.
- SQL push-down: no code in the diff, nothing to judge.
- Limit of this review: the ruling was made in the seat thread, which is not on GitHub and is not an input here. The quotes were compared with the fleet's GitHub records of it, not with the thread itself. The Note says as much ("in the seat thread", "the card bodies quote him"). The maintainer lands this PR himself (Tier H) and is the reader who can confirm his own words.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**The maintainer's words.** All four quoted strings match their sources byte for byte, with the right UTC time beside each:

| Quote in the Note | Time | Found in |
|---|---|---|
| 「我觉得这个应该是一个元数据的配置项吧，这种应该是常见需求。」 | 03:36Z | bodies of #37800, #37792, #37802 |
| 「我能够具体配置每一个页签显示哪些分组吗？然后还有一个开关控制第一个页面要不要pin到左侧」 | 03:40Z | bodies of #37800, #37792, #37802 |
| 「是否建议保留 relatedList 这个语法」 | 03:51Z | bodies of #37800, #37792, #37802 |
| 「例外 + 新键 fieldTabs」 | 04:07Z decision card | the three bodies and comment 7209608089 |

Comment 7209608089 is on #37792 and 7209632085 is on #37800, as the two links say. 7209632085 carries no words of the ruling: it reads "filed per Jack 04:07Z decision card". The Note calls both "records" and adds "the card bodies quote him", which is accurate.

**The ruling, restated.**

- `pinOverview` covers the wide full page only: holds. Card #37800 says "desktop full standard record page only: whether the overview pins left". On `main`, `recordPagePinsDetails` (`ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/synth/recordPageColumns.ts`) returns false off a full page and under `RECORD_PAGE_PIN_MIN_WIDTH`, so "the side preview and a phone never pin" and "pinning is otherwise derived" are both true of the code. The Note names the synthesized (default) record page, so an authored page is outside it. Neither wider nor narrower.
- `fieldTabs` are the tabs after the overview: holds. Card #37800 says "named field groups drawn as tabs right after the overview; `relatedLists` unchanged". The Note adds "in declared order, ahead of every other tab", which is #37802's placement rule (step 3) and follows from "right after". It does not fix the entry shape or the v1 refusals, which stay on #37802.
- Separation from `FormSchema.fieldTabs`: holds. `FormSchema` in `ui/packages/types/src/form.ts` declares `fieldTabs`, `defaultFieldTab` and `fieldTabsPosition`; `ui/packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx` reads `schema.fieldTabs` and its comment says it "spreads THIS form's fields across tab panels". No `fieldTabs` exists in `packages/spec` on `main`, so the two cannot be confused in the spec today.
- Every other key still needs its own ruling: holds. Card #37800 asks for exactly this sentence. It keeps the closing line of the `actionLayout` Note ("The guard keeps its force for every other key, above all per-page show/hide switches") and covers hide-only as well as re-arrange-only keys, which is §2's own pair.

**Agreement with ADR-0085 on `main`.** "The 2026-11-23 note counts two places" is what that Note says ("There are now two places"). Like it, this Note calls the keys ruled exceptions and does not claim they pass the admission test; "each only re-arranges one surface" is the honest reading against test 2. "Field tabs are a sibling key, not entries in it" leaves the 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-22 Notes on `relatedLists` as they read. "The synthesized (default) record page" is the 2026-11-22 addendum's own term. The Note cites no other ADR.

**Anchors, symbols, ids.** `recordPagePinsDetails` is exported from the cited file; `ui/packages/types/src/form.ts` exists and holds the three named members; issues #37800, #37792 and #37802 exist and are open; both comment ids resolve to the issues their links name. No line-number anchor is written.

**Length.** Earned. The Note is 30 lines against 19 because it carries two keys, three dated quotes plus the choice, and one thing the `actionLayout` Note had no need for: the homonym with the form-level key, which is a real collision (20 files under `ui/`). The sentence on the 03:51Z question is the only candidate to trim, and the card asked for "`relatedLists` unchanged" to be stated.

Nits (none affects the contract):

- N1 (nit) — "the 概览 tab". On `main` the first tab's label is 「详情」 / Details (`detail.recordTabOverview` in `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/zh-Hans.ts` and `en.ts`, and the header of `recordPageColumns.ts`: "the details as its first tab, 「详情」"). Code comments and the cards still say 概览, and the tab's value is `details`, so the reader is not misled about which tab is meant, but the label is not the one the page draws.
- N2 (nit) — "His 「是否建议保留 relatedList 这个语法」 (03:51Z) ended with `relatedLists` kept, unrenamed and unchanged: field tabs are a sibling key". Comment 7209360806 on #37792 (03:53Z) shows what that exchange ended with: the name kept, and a design that still put a field-tab entry inside `relatedLists`. "Unchanged" and the sibling key come from the 04:07Z choice. The end state the sentence gives is true; the step it credits is one too early.
- N3 (nit) — "Neither key is in the spec yet" is true today and dated, but goes stale when #37792 and #37802 land. The `actionLayout` Note ends "Built by #36629". Each implementing card should add its own "built by" line when it lands; neither card says so yet.

One reading to keep in view on #37792, not a finding here: the Note says `pinOverview` "says whether the overview pins", which is the maintainer's 03:40Z wording. The card gives the key one effective value in v1 (`false` stops pinning; absent or `true` is today's derived rule). The Note does not say `true` forces a pin where the derived rule would not, and #37792 must not read it that way.

## Contract review brief — PR #38010 @ `33b946d34d087b6a60e3a1a5e3ac6d3f64f8f98c` (card #37800)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths docs/adr/0085-object-semantic-roles-over-surface-hint-blocks.md` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #37800: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #38010: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `30a8047bad6e264762dd41ded7f1290c1224afc6` (the merge base)
  · the check-runs on `33b946d34d087b6a60e3a1a5e3ac6d3f64f8f98c`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: docs/adr/0085-object-semantic-roles-over-surface-hint-blocks.md;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

Security — a `hits` path sits on the low-risk skills arm: when the change teaches security, auth or permission
  behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label.
  The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed
  hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, else `yes`.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/166e2125-4268-552f-a555-2b7c43a99f0f/scratchpad/pr-38010/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.
